validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE: real, independently confirmed, correctly classified as an operating intrastate transmission lateral segment (not gathering, not a duplicate). Five independent-of-Enterprise sources plus Enterprise's own corporate-history statement all describe the SAME 80-ish-mile lateral running from near Alexandria, LA to third-party interconnects near Gillis, LA, built to move Haynesville Shale gas to Gulf Coast LNG facilities: Pipeline & Gas Journal (2019-09-20, proposal announcement, via Wayback since the live URL 404s), AEGIS Hedging (energy risk advisory, ~2020/2021, explicitly names it 'Acadian Gillis Lateral'), Oil & Gas Journal (2023-05-31 title and 2021-12-16 in-service story), Natural Gas Intelligence (2021-12-15, in-service story), LNGprime (2021-12-16, in-service story), and Enterprise's own 'Our History' page (still live, 200 OK). All five in-service-era sources agree the lateral: (a) is named 'Gillis Lateral'; (b) runs from near Alexandria to interconnects near Gillis, LA (matches GEM StartPrefecture/District=Alexandria exactly, State=Louisiana both ends); (c) carries ~1 Bcf/d = 1000 MMcf/d (matches GEM Capacity=1000.00 MMcf/d exactly); (d) entered commercial service December 2021 (matches GEM StartYear1=2021/StartMonth1=12 exactly); (e) is owned/operated by Enterprise Products Partners (matches GEM Owner1=Enterprise Products Partners, 100%). CHECKED AGAINST THE ROSTER for duplicate/relabel: P3283 is NOT the same asset as P0143 (Acadian system, aggregate/umbrella entity, len=1000mi as originally acquired in 2000 -- now stale, see cross_row_leads) or P5709 (Haynesville Extension, the older 270-mile trunk built 2009-2011 that the Gillis Lateral extends FROM, per Enterprise's own history page and the 2009 OGJ announcement). These are three genuinely distinct physical assets on a shared corridor -- P3283 is the newest, smallest, most specific of the three, not a re-labeling of either. CAVEAT (length rounding): GEM's LengthKnown=83.00mi is an exact match to Enterprise's own history page ('The 83-mile Gillis Lateral pipeline...'); every trade-press source instead rounds to 'approximately 80-mile'. This is rounding, not a material disagreement -- both figures describe the same segment. Opened and read to exhaustion: all 5 in-service-era articles plus the 2019 proposal article plus Enterprise's own history page (searched for diameter, pressure, construction start, and segment cost in every one -- see fills; none of the 8 sources state those four values for this specific segment, only for the parent Haynesville Extension trunk, which would be an aggregate-vs-segment mismatch to borrow from).

Pipeline & Gas Journal, dated Sep 20 2019 (matches ProposalYear/Month exactly): 'Enterprise plans to construct an 80-mile, 1-Bcf/d intrastate pipeline originating near Cheneyville, Louisiana, on its Acadian Haynesville Extension to third-party interconnects near Gillis...capacity by 300 MMcf/d--to 2.1 Bcf/d from 1.8 Bcf/d...expected to begin service in mid-2021.' The project is not yet named 'Gillis Lateral' at this pre-construction stage (that name is first attested in the AEGIS Hedging piece and the 2021 in-service coverage), so url_verifier's --name check correctly returns name_found=false. Hand-confirmed as the SAME project by an exact fingerprint match against the later-named coverage: identical route (near Alexandria/Cheneyville to Gillis), identical capacity (1 Bcf/d lateral / +300 MMcf/d net to the Acadian system, 1.8->2.1 Bcf/d), identical compressor station (Mansfield, DeSoto Parish), identical mid-2021-ish target (actual: Dec 2021).

fills.researcher_notes: Single dated source for the exact Sep-2019 proposal date; the page itself never uses the name 'Gillis Lateral' (project unnamed at announcement), so it is capped at medium per the sweep gates even though the project-identity match is confident. Searched for a second dated proposal announcement (Enterprise investor-day slide decks, SEC filings, a second trade-press outlet) and found none earlier than or contemporaneous with the Sep 2019 PGJ piece -- AEGIS Hedging's article corroborates the same project by name and numbers but carries no explicit proposal date of its own, so it doesn't count as a second date-bearing source.

Searched all 8 sources in the pool (PGJ 2019 proposal, AEGIS Hedging, OGJ x2, NGI, LNGprime, the Enterprise/txgulf.org press-release mirror, Enterprise's own history page) plus an open-web search for 'Gillis Lateral construction began/groundbreaking 2020 OR 2021' -- none states a construction-start date, only the Sep-2019 proposal and the Dec-2021 in-service date. AEGIS's undated (~2020/2021) piece uses present-tense 'Enterprise is constructing' but gives no year of its own beyond its 2021 in-service estimate. Left UNRESOLVED rather than guess a year from the proposal-to-in-service window.

cross_row_leads.facts: Enterprise completed a 400-MMcfd expansion of the Acadian Haynesville Extension pipeline on 2023-05-31, increasing its capacity to 2.5 Bcf/d. Combined with the Dec-2021 Gillis Lateral project's own +300 MMcf/d Mansfield compressor uprate (1.8->2.1 Bcf/d), P5709's roster capacity of 1800 MMcf/d looks stale -- current capacity per Enterprise's own disclosures is 2500 MMcf/d, not 1800. (Independently corroborates the same finding already staged in P0143.json's cross_row_leads.)

This 2023-05-31 article is very likely the direct source for P5401 (Acadian Gas Pipeline System, capacity expansion, Capacity=400.00, LengthKnown=0.0, LastUpdated=2023-07-07): 'Enterprise Products Partners has completed a 400-MMcfd expansion of its Acadian Haynesville Extension natural gas pipeline, increasing its capacity to 2.5 bcfd,' compression-only (Mansfield compressor station), consistent with P5401's LengthKnown=0/no new pipe.

'The Legacy Acadian and Haynesville Extension pipelines are part of the Acadian Gas Pipeline system, which comprises 1,300 miles of gas pipelines...' (as of Dec 2021) -- vs. P0143's roster LengthKnown=1000mi, which reflects the ~1,000-mile figure from the original 2000 acquisition. The system has grown via the Haynesville Extension (2011) and Gillis Lateral (2021) additions since then; P0143's length may need updating to ~1,300mi if it's meant to track the current aggregate system rather than the as-acquired legacy footprint.

summary: P3283 (Acadian Gillis Lateral) is real, correctly classified, not a duplicate of P0143 or P5709, and independently corroborated on name/length/capacity/start-date/location/owner/operator by 5+ mutually-independent sources; Diameter/Pressure/ConstructionYear/SegmentCost stay UNRESOLVED after an exhaustive search of the full citation pool plus open-web search turned up nothing segment-specific.
